chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man drank wine during the time of Abu Bakr, so it was brought to Abu Bakr. He said to him, 'Did you drink wine?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'And why, while it is prohibited?' The man said to him, 'I embraced Islam, and my Islam was good, and my home is among a people who drink wine and consider it permissible. Had I known that it was forbidden, I would have avoided it.'

Abu Bakr turned to Umar and said, 'What do you say regarding the matter of this man?' Umar said, 'It is a perplexing matter, and there is none for it except Abu al-Hasan.' So Abu Bakr said, 'Call Ali for us.' Umar said, 'The judge is summoned from his home.'

So they stood up, with the man and those present among the people accompanying them, until they came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). They informed him of the man's story, and the man recounted his own story.

He said, 'Send with him someone who will go around with him to the gatherings of the Emigrants and the Helpers; whoever recited the Verse of Prohibition to him, let him testify against him.' So they did that with him, but no one testified against him that he had recited the Verse of Prohibition to him. So he freed him and said to him, 'If you drink after this, we will establish the Hadd (penalty) upon you.'

key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: The Emigrants (early Muslims who migrated to Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for imposing the Hadd penalty for drinking wine in early Islamic history?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia scholarly principle of 'Tasbit al-Hukm' (establishing the ruling) through the actual transmission of the revelation, rather than mere general knowledge of the Prophet's authority. By requiring witnesses to confirm the man heard the specific Verse of Prohibition, Ali ibn Abi Talib emphasized that legal accountability (Taklif) is contingent upon the recipient's awareness of the divine command, a nuance often highlighted in Usuli jurisprudence. This incident serves as a foundational precedent for distinguishing between the existence of a ruling and its applicability to an individual based on their reception of the evidence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man drank the wine in the era of Abu Bakr, so it was raised to Abu Bakr. So said to him, ‘Did you drink the wine?’ He said, ‘Yes’. He said, ‘And why did you, and it is Prohibited?’ So the man said to him, ‘I became a Muslim, and my Islam was good, and my house is among a people who are drinking the wine, and they are permitting it, and had I know that it is Prohibited, I would have kept away from it’.

So Abu Bakr turned to Umar, so he said, ‘So what are you saying regarding the matter of this man?’ So Umar said, ‘And there is none for it except for Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>’. So Abu Bakr said, ‘Call Ali<sup>asws</sup> for us’. So Umar said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> gives the judgement in his<sup>asws</sup> home’.

So they both stood up, and the man was with the two of them, along with the ones who were present with them both, until they all came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>. So they informed him of the story of the man, and the man related his own story.

So heasws said: ‘Send (some people) with him who would go around with him at the gatherings of the Emigrants and the Helpers, (to find) one who had recited to him the Verse of the Prophibition, so let him testify against him’. So they did that with him, but no one testified against him that he had recited the Verse of the Prohibition to him. So heasws freed him and said to him: ‘If you drink wine after it, we would establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon you’.
